newsitem.title: CANADA: Placer Dome sees improved Q1 results.
newsitem.headline: Placer Dome sees improved Q1 results.

text.p: Placer Dome Inc said on Tuesday that its gold output rose in the first quarter, while its production cost fell, and that its quarterly earnings would improve.
Chief Executive John Willson told the annual meeting that a preliminary tally put first-quarter gold production at 530,000 ounces, up from 476,000 ounces in the fourth quarter.

Placer's cash production cost dropped to US$225 an ounce from US$238 in the fourth quarter. Willson said the quarterly production rate would rise through the year, and the company repeated its 1997 production forecast of 2.3 million ounces.
Asked about the outlook for first-quarter results, Willson told reporters, "...our earnings will obviously improve."
"On the other hand, we've seen the price of gold go down. Happily we are substantially hedged against that. But nonetheless our realized price will drop considerably with gold dropping."
Placer is due to release its first quarter results on April 23.
Willson told the annual meeting that after concentrating on growth in its production, Placer's top priority was to improve its financial performance.
He noted that the company's share price had languished compared to its peers and said improved an financial performance would boost the shares.
Willson reiterated Placer's contention that its claim to the Las Cristinas property in Venezuela is secure despite an ownership dispute with Crystallex International Corp.
Arbitration is continuing with Kazakhstan over Placer's attempts to recover US$35 million paid to the government there for a now-abandoned mining project.
Placer has not given up hope of recouping the money either as cash or in mineral properties or exploration rights.
Willson estimated that Placer spent about US$1.5 million in its pursuit of Bre-X Minerals Ltd and its Busang gold property in Indonesia.
